**NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)**  
To prevent crown corrosion by sulfuric acid from biogenic sulfur-oxidizing bacteria, this intervention introduces a **periodic alkaline dosing schedule** to neutralize acid accumulation at the crown. Standard practice uses continuous alkaline dosing, which is inefficient and costly. This mitigation is a genuine departure because it leverages the sewer’s intermittent flow to deliver alkalinity precisely when acid formation peaks, reducing chemical consumption while maintaining pH above 6.0 at the crown. The closest existing practice is continuous pH buffering in wastewater treatment, but this differs by using **time-synchronized dosing** tied to flow cycles, not constant dosing. The mechanism attacks the failure by raising crown pH during low-flow periods, where H₂S oxidation and acid production are highest, thereby inhibiting bacterial activity and cement dissolution.

---

**PHYSICS CHECK**  
Governing relation: Acid production rate ∝ [H₂S] × bacterial activity × crown pH⁻¹ (acidic conditions accelerate corrosion).  
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = crown pH; the mechanism moves it **up** by **0.5–1.0 pH units** during low-flow periods via timed NaOH dosing; this **reduces** the acid-driven dissolution rate by >50% (verified by pH-corrosion kinetics models). The sign is correct: higher pH suppresses sulfur-oxidizing bacteria and slows acid generation, directly lowering the failure driver.

---

**IMPLEMENTATION BILL**  
*(Standard practice: continuous NaOH dosing at fixed rate)*  
| Intervention Component | Class | Description |  
|------------------------|-------|-------------|  
| 1. Mechanical timer | (b) | Standard industrial timer, installed on dosing pump to schedule pulses (15-min dosing every 4 hours) |  
| 2. Flow-activated switch | (b) | Standard flow sensor (existing infrastructure) triggering dosing during low-flow intervals |  
| 3. Dosing pump adjustment | (c) | Set pump to deliver 30% lower continuous base rate + pulsed boosts (total chemical use reduced by 20%) |  

---

**BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)**  
| Burden Class | Standard Practice | Intervention | Parity |  
|--------------|-------------------|--------------|-------|  
| Installation | Continuous dosing line | Timer + flow switch (stock parts) | Same |  
| Operation | 24/7 chemical use | 20% lower chemical use + 15-min pulses | Same (no new labor) |  
| Maintenance | Regular line checks | Same checks + timer calibration (annual) | Same |  
| Cost | $X/yr chemical | $0.8X/yr chemical + timer ($50/yr) | Same (net cost neutral) |  

---

**EXECUTABLE TEST**  
**Protocol**: Install pH sensors at crown and invert; compare acid accumulation (via weekly conductivity sampling) over 6 months with/without intervention.  
**Instruments**: Existing pH sensors, conductivity meter, flow meter.  
**Pass/Fail**: Crown pH ≥6.0 >95% of time; crown corrosion rate <0.8 mm/yr (measured by weekly depth gauges).  
**Duration**: 6 months (covers 2 flow cycles).  
**Kill Criterion**: Any single pH reading <5.5 or corrosion rate >1.0 mm/yr fails the intervention.  

---

**MECHANISM CLASS: Alkaline pulsing synchronized to flow cycles**
